name: Band Pull-Apart (Underhand Grip)
description: The underhand (supinated) grip band pull-apart shifts emphasis from the overhand version toward the lower trapezius and posterior deltoid, while also incorporating greater biceps tendon stress and external rotation. The supinated grip forces the humeral head into a more externally rotated position throughout the movement, which can be both a corrective exercise cue for those with internally rotated posture and a tool for targeting slightly different scapular retractor fibers than the standard overhand pull-apart.

execution.starting_position: Hold a resistance band with an underhand (supinated) grip, hands shoulder-width apart, arms extended in front at shoulder height. Palms face the ceiling.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a light resistance band. The supinated grip is the defining feature — ensure palms face up throughout the movement.
steps: Step 1: Hold the band underhand at shoulder height, arms extended.
Step 2: Pull the band apart by moving the arms outward and backward.
Step 3: Continue until the band touches the chest, maintaining the supinated grip.
Step 4: Squeeze the scapulae together and hold for a moment.
Step 5: Return under control to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you pull apart, inhale as you return.
common_mistakes: Letting the grip rotate to neutral or pronated during the pull
Using a band that is too heavy, causing the elbows to bend excessively
safety_considerations: Ensure the band is in good condition before use — worn bands can snap
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Band starts at shoulder height with arms forward, pulled to chest-contact at the rear.
coaching_cues: Palms face up the whole time
Feel the scapulae squeeze at the end
